steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Context: The Historic Environment is a compulsory part of the Elizabethan England GCSE paper. Each year, the exam board specifies a particular Elizabethan site that students must study. The site changes every year, so you need to check which site is specified for your exam year. The Historic Environment question tests your ability to connect a physical place to the broader themes of Elizabethan history - understanding not just what a building looked like, but why it was built, what it tells us about Elizabethan society, and how it connects to the wider events of the period. | Prodigy Houses: The Elizabethan era saw the construction of enormous, lavishly decorated houses by wealthy courtiers.
